question: I heard that people with behavioral health conditions smoke more. Is that true?
answer: Yes, individuals with behavioral health conditions account for 38% of all U.S. adult cigarette consumption, even though they only make up 25% of the population. Their smoking rate is 23%, which is higher than the general adult rate of 14%.
